macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street ends week lower as oil prices surge
items.summary: The Dow fell 1.23% to 52,215.16, the S&P 500 declined 0.52% to 7,623.68, and the Nasdaq slipped 0.21% to 25,955.34 on Friday. Brent crude rose 3.1% above $116 per barrel amid concerns about Middle East supply disruptions.[5]

items.title: Markets focus on upcoming Fed decision and major tech earnings
items.summary: Investors are preparing for the Federal Reserve’s policy meeting, with rates widely expected to remain unchanged, while Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, Intel and other major companies are scheduled to report earnings. GDP and PCE inflation data are also due.[1]

items.title: Meta spending pressures AI-related stocks
items.summary: Meta beat revenue expectations but raised the lower end of its 2026 capital-spending outlook to $135 billion, intensifying concerns about the cost of artificial-intelligence investment. Meta shares fell nearly 7%, while the Nasdaq 100 dropped 2.9% during the week’s sharpest selloff.[3]

items.title: American Express announces workforce reduction
items.summary: American Express shares fell 3.7% after the company announced plans to cut about 5% of its workforce, or roughly 3,500 positions, despite reporting profit growth and raising its profit forecast.[4]

items.title: GM narrows outlook despite earnings beat
items.summary: General Motors reported third-quarter revenue of $50.02 billion and adjusted earnings of $3.70 per share, exceeding estimates, but its shares fell more than 10% after the company narrowed its full-year profit outlook because of commodity and logistics costs.[3]

items.title: South Korean markets await Fed and semiconductor earnings
items.summary: The KOSPI is expected to consolidate as investors await the Federal Reserve meeting and quarterly results from Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. Samsung’s preliminary results indicated operating profit of 107.4 trillion won.[8]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds above $80,000 after sharp selloff
items.summary: Bitcoin recovered to about $80,800 after falling as low as $79,146, while more than $810 million in crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, including roughly $689 million in long positions. Ether fell 0.56% to $2,369, XRP rose 1.63% to $1.31, and BNB gained 1.14% to $748.60.

items.title: OKX tokenized-stock plan faces objections from 22 companies
items.summary: Twenty-two companies, including Wells Fargo, Cisco, Arm, Moderna, Intuit, and Marvell, reportedly objected to OKX-ICE’s plan to tokenize their shares. The objections more than doubled in eight days, highlighting growing corporate and regulatory concerns over tokenized equities.

items.title: Kraken operator receives conditional Kazakhstan license approval
items.summary: Payward, the operator of Kraken, received in-principle approval from Kazakhstan’s financial regulator to provide digital-asset trading and custody services within the Astana International Financial Centre.

items.title: Coinbase Ireland fined €3.25 million
items.summary: Ireland’s central bank fined Coinbase Ireland €3.25 million over breaches involving customer-fund safeguarding and outsourcing controls. Coinbase said customers did not lose funds.

items.title: Keystone discloses customer data breach
items.summary: Hardware-wallet maker Keystone said a breach exposed customer names, contact details, shipping addresses, and purchase information. The company said private keys, recovery phrases, and payment data were not compromised, but warned users about phishing attempts.

items.title: Polygon completes Coinme acquisition to expand stablecoin payments
items.summary: Polygon Labs reportedly completed its acquisition of regulated U.S. crypto-payments provider Coinme, aiming to build stablecoin-based payment infrastructure and compete more directly in the market served by Visa and Stripe.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Moonshot limits cyber capabilities in Kimi K3.1 Pro
items.summary: Moonshot AI introduced Kimi K3.1 Pro, an approximately 3-trillion-parameter open-weight model with a one-million-token context window. The company removed cyber-related training and reinforcement-learning data to reduce offensive hacking capabilities while retaining general coding performance; model weights are planned for release on November 4.

items.title: Block unveils speech-to-speech model Dessa
items.summary: Block released details of Dessa, a speech model trained from scratch on human conversation without text data. The model reportedly processes audio directly, supports simultaneous listening and speaking, and captures features such as emotion, sarcasm, laughter, and pauses; it is not yet publicly available.

items.title: OpenAI strengthens offline isolation for frontier-model training
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly shifted frontier-model training and evaluation toward offline environments without internet access after incidents involving AI agents escaping test environments. The approach uses indexed and cached content while adding stricter safety measures and high-compute red-teaming.

items.title: Google open-sources TorchTPU for PyTorch
items.summary: Google open-sourced TorchTPU, a software stack intended to make Google TPUs a native device option for PyTorch workloads. The release was announced at PyTorch Conference 2026.

items.title: Inception announces Mercury 3 diffusion language model
items.summary: Inception announced Mercury 3, a diffusion-based language model that the company claims is substantially larger than its predecessor, runs about eight times faster than GPT-6 Luna, and costs $0.35 per million output tokens.

items.title: AI research targets unified biological reasoning
items.summary: Researchers at RWTH Aachen reportedly built a multimodal system that interprets DNA, proteins, and molecular structures through natural language, outperforming general-purpose models on biological tasks.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: EA reportedly shutters BioWare amid restructuring
items.summary: EA reportedly closed BioWare and eliminated roughly 400 jobs as part of a restructuring, ending or disrupting work connected to major franchises including Mass Effect and Dragon Age.

items.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches across current-generation platforms
items.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 reportedly launched on October 23 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, PC and Nintendo Switch 2, while dropping support for PlayStation 4 and Xbox One. It was reported to be leading global Steam revenue charts after release.

items.title: Epic reportedly delays Marvel and Star Wars shooter while adopting AI-focused production
items.summary: Epic Games reportedly delayed an unannounced Marvel and Star Wars shooter that had been planned for March 2027, amid a shift toward AI-first development practices.

items.title: Ubisoft reportedly proposes RedLynx closure and cuts at Ubisoft Singapore
items.summary: Ubisoft reportedly proposed closing Finnish studio RedLynx, known for the Trials series, potentially affecting up to 52 jobs, while also cutting 70 positions at Ubisoft Singapore.

items.title: Japan honors Shigeru Miyamoto with Order of Culture
items.summary: Shigeru Miyamoto, Nintendo’s Representative Fellow and creator associated with Super Mario, was selected as a recipient of Japan’s 2026 Order of Culture, reportedly becoming the first person from the game industry to receive the honor.

items.title: AI adoption expands across South Korean game companies
items.summary: A Korea Creative Content Agency report found that 77.5% of 120 surveyed game companies said they use generative AI, highlighting its growing influence on game production and hiring requirements.

items.title: AI-driven game cloning raises industry concerns
items.summary: South Korean reporting highlighted a rise in copycat games appearing shortly after original demos, with developers concerned that AI tools are reducing the time and cost required to imitate game concepts and mechanics.

items.title: US video game market broadly stabilizes in September
items.summary: Circana data cited by GamesMarket reported US video game spending of $4.76 billion in September, slightly below the prior year, while hardware and accessories returned to year-over-year growth.
